attributes.axis_log: A0 BASELINE probe real 465 (insns 1138 target / 1139 ours, multiset 43t); defake_gate baseline game/sfx/psfx.c = 13 fns, 8 at real 0; webfrank screen = only DoPlyrSfxSub pinned in this TU and it neither calls PlayerSfxInitData nor uses the swap helpers, so no pinned body or pinned-inlinee closure is in scope. A1 DEFINITION-ORDER VERDICT (the lever the work_claim named as untried, screened FIRST and REFUTED BY TARGET EVIDENCE before any edit): config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt gives the target .text order PlayerSfxClearData 0x8008A584 < PlayerSfxInitData 0x8008A5F4 < fn_8008A678 0x8008A678 < ClearAllPlyrData 0x8008A82C < ClearPlyrData 0x8008A898 < LoadPlyrData 0x8008A928 < LoadPdataFile 0x8008BAF0, and our psfx.c defines those seven in EXACTLY that order already. Retail therefore placed PlayerSfxInitData BEFORE LoadPlyrData and STILL emitted `bl` -- so being defined-before-use is NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT for MWCC to inline, the defined-before rule is NOT the mechanism here, and moving the definition below LoadPlyrData would both contradict retail's own layout and bar the TU from ever promoting to Matching. No edit was made on this axis. A2 `#pragma inline_max_auto_size(0)` around LoadPlyrData -> NEUTRAL, byte-identical (real 465, 43t). A3 free-falsification control `#pragma inline_max_size(0)` -> also NEUTRAL and byte-identical, which is decisive: had that pragma been honoured it would have collapsed all 70 explicit swap-helper inline expansions into calls. Nothing moved, so the whole inline_max_* family is SILENTLY IGNORED by this compiler (no diagnostic emitted). Axis closed by control, not by guesswork. A4 `#pragma auto_inline off` around the CALLER (LoadPlyrData) -> NEUTRAL, byte-identical: auto-inline candidacy is not decided at the call site. A5 `#pragma auto_inline off/on` around the CALLEE'S OWN DEFINITION (PlayerSfxInitData, psfx.c:1070-1090) -> IMPROVED real 465 -> 387, insns 1138/1139, multiset 43t -> 5t. Both `bl PlayerSfxInitData` landed, the swap helpers stayed inlined, and critically PlayerSfxInitData's own bytes were UNCHANGED (still real 0) -- the exact outcome the dont_inline form could not produce, since it grew that callee's frame 48 -> 56. defake_gate GATE OK, 1 improved, 0 regressions. COMMITTED 234d122d6. A6 remaining residual localised by aligned fnasm to three clusters, all in the entry region: (i) ours-only `mr` at 0x2c, (ii) target `bge ->48` + `b ->11b4` vs our single `blt` at 0x40, (iii) ours-only `add` at 0x2cc. A7 cluster (ii) worked per claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge: the unconditional targets the merged epilogue at 0x11b4, so this is the FORWARD (source-reachable) variant. Merging the two entry guards into the short-circuit form `if (plr < 0 || cls < 0) { return; }` reproduced the target's branch pair EXACTLY and drove the opcode multiset 5t -> 2t with `target-only: (none)` -- i.e. we became a strict superset of the target's opcode stream. But it cost one extra instruction (1139 -> 1140 vs target 1138) and scored WORSE on both project metrics: real 387 -> 412 and objdiff fuzzy 98.4244% -> 98.3893%. ARBITRATED per the CONFLICT rule with a full ninja + report on each side rather than on the --ops cluster alone: reverted to the two-separate-guards form. Recorded so the next agent does not re-derive it -- this is the mirror image of claim.law.guard-polarity-restructure-fixes-count-parity-not-form, where reproducing the target's local branch FORM is a genuine structural gain that the whole-function metrics nonetheless reject. A8 cluster (iii): the `add` at 0x2cc rematerialises pdata+plr*4 (already held from 0x4c) so the loop at psfx.c:1286 can load `128(r3)`, where the target reloads `0(r31)` through a live `&pdata->headers[plr]`. Probed the matching spelling -- a block-scope `void** hdrSlot = &pdata->headers[plr];` with `p = (u8*)*hdrSlot + off;`. REGRESSED real 412 -> 413: naming the slot materialised an EXTRA `addi` and the rematerialised `add` PERSISTED, which is the informative part -- the address FORM is not the discriminator, the allocator's refusal to keep the base live across the two MBGetFromWad calls is. Reverted. Cluster (iii) is the same identical source expression `pdata->headers[plr]` that compiles correctly at psfx.c:1275-1278, so it is a liveness/rematerialisation decision, not a spelling one.

attributes.residual: IMPROVED, not exact. Best retained: real 465 -> 387, objdiff fuzzy 94.259224% -> 98.4244%, insns 1138 target / 1139 ours, opcode multiset 5 tokens. The residual is TWO extra instructions, both named and both allocator-driven, plus one balanced reorder. (i) ours-only `mr` at 0x2c: `lis r3,lbl_802828B0@ha; addi r0,r3,@lo; mr r25,r0` where the target forms the pointer directly into its callee-saved home as `addi r27,r3,@lo`. This is a THIRD independent instance of claim.law.addr16-lo-address-homed-via-r0-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1, whose two prior instances were both in pmotion.c against lbl_80282850; this one is psfx.c against lbl_802828B0, confirming the mechanism is global rather than pmotion-local. Per that law's explicit disposition no source probe was spent on it. (ii) ours-only `add` at 0x2cc: rematerialisation of pdata+plr*4 across two MBGetFromWad calls where the target keeps `&pdata->headers[plr]` live in r31; the source spelling is already identical to the sites that DO match (psfx.c:1275-1278), and A8 proved naming the slot only adds an `addi`. (iii) a balanced `li`/`mtctr` reorder at 0x56c and 0x6cc-0x6e0 that contributes nothing to the opcode multiset (pure SCHEDULE). NOT WEBFRANK-ELIGIBLE as it stands: the two residual words are EXTRA INSTRUCTIONS, not recolourings or permutations, so the register and permute stages cannot express them -- cf. claim.law.unpaired-schedule-words-bar-webfrank-candidacy-not-just-its-permute-stage.20260831.v1. Closing (ii) would leave a single unpaired `mr` and might then reduce to a bijection; that is the one remaining path to exact and it needs an allocator-pressure idea, not another spelling.
